issues.description: setuptools<82 added as runtime dependency in core extras leaks CI workaround into user installs
issues.detail: Adding 'setuptools<82' under core/setup.py 'raytune' extras (or similar extra) forces every user installing this extra to downgrade setuptools system-wide. The cap exists only for mmcv CI builds; pinning it in published wheels affects unrelated environments and can conflict with other packages requiring modern setuptools. Should live only in the CI script.

issues.description: mmdet bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 without justification or compatibility check
issues.detail: The PR title says 'Fix mmengine failure', but mmdet is also upgraded a minor version. mmdet 3.3.0 may have different API/behavior than 3.2.0 and could break downstream multimodal/detection code paths. The bump should either be reverted or called out with a reason and tested coverage.

issues.description: mmcv installed with --no-build-isolation may pull wrong torch/build env
issues.detail: Switching from 'mim install mmcv==2.1.0' to 'pip install mmcv==2.1.0 --no-build-isolation' compiles against the ambient environment. If torch or CUDA toolkit aren't already present at install time, the build will fail or produce a CPU-only/incompatible extension. The previous mim path handled this; the new ordering needs torch pre-installed.

issues.description: Duplicate setuptools<82 pin in build_pkg and setup_mmcv is redundant and drift-prone
issues.detail: Both env_setup.sh build_pkg and setup_mmcv.sh re-pin setuptools<82. When the upstream mmcv issue is fixed, both spots must be reverted in sync; the FIXME comments reference the same issue but live in three files (including core/setup.py). Consider a single shared variable or central pin.

issues.description: Install order may leave mmengine version unconstrained during mmcv build
issues.detail: mmcv 2.1.0 is installed before mmengine 0.10.7. If mmcv's build/runtime pulls a different mmengine transitively, the later explicit install may downgrade/upgrade in a way that breaks the already-built extension's expectations. Installing mmengine first or pinning both in one pip call is safer.

review.summary: This PR works around an upstream mmcv/setuptools incompatibility by capping setuptools<82 and switching MMEngine from a git pin to a PyPI release. The main concern is that the setuptools cap leaked into core/setup.py as a runtime dependency, which affects end users, not just CI. Additionally, mmdet was bumped to 3.3.0 without explanation, and the new mmcv install uses --no-build-isolation which depends on prior torch availability. The triple-pinning of setuptools across three files creates maintenance drift when the upstream fix lands.
